subject: Adding a covariate to a dsm

messages.author: 4391a11a04482aae
messages.subject: Adding a covariate to a dsm
parts:
Hai guys,

I have been following the mexico dolphins example to develop dsm for some parrot species here in Zambia. I finally fitted two models and am now trying to add a covariate of Transect type (I had walking and driving transects) but am stuck with this error;
dsm.obj.T_Type <- dsm(count~s(X,Y,k=10) + s(T_Type,k=20), detfc.hr.null, segment.data = segment.data_new, observation.data = obsdata,method = "REML")
Error in names(dat) <- object$term :
  'names' attribute [1] must be the same length as the vector [0]

The Data:  I have segmented my transects into 0.5km which is 4860 rows of segments (segment.data) and I had 192 rows of observations (observation.data) - i used the same sample labelling in both, with the 192 of course not having each of the 4860 rows, only those with presence records - could this be the problem? and how can i get around it?

Chaona

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Adding a covariate to a dsm
parts:
Chaona

Without seeing more details about your data and analysis, I can only comment literally about the error message. From your note, you suggest you were able to successfully fit dsm models without the transect type covariate. Check whether the transect type field exists in both the segment.data and the observation.data and check that the field name "T_Type" is applied consistently in segment.data, observation.data and in the data that went into the detection function model fitting.

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Adding a covariate to a dsm
parts:
Chaona

Having transect type in your dsm model doesn't make sense. Remember, you will use the covariates in your dsm model to predict to places you didn't visit in your study area. Transect type is undefined for areas not sampled.
From: 'Eric Rexstad' via distance-sampling <distance...@googlegroups.com>
Sent: 21 February 2023 13:59
To: chaona phiri <chaon...@gmail.com>

Cc: distance...@googlegroups.com <distance...@googlegroups.com>
Subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Adding a covariate to a dsm

Your T_Type is a factor covariate (only taking on two possible values). You can't fit a smooth to that. You could add a term "as.factor(T_Type)" to your model. Have a read through some of the mgcv​ documentation.
